factories.name: createDrag
factories.capability: A page author turns a container's direct children into a list a person reorders by dragging with the pointer, with a drop-position indicator and an optional drag handle. The same factory adds click, Ctrl-click, and Shift-click multi-selection, and it drags the selected set as one group.
factories.api: `createDrag<T>(element, options?)` returns `CreateDragInstance`: readonly refs `dragging`, `indices`, `selected`, `target`, and `position`, plus the methods `select`, `tap` (the same function as `select`), `clear`, and `destroy` (elements/src/browser/factories/createDrag.ts:482-492). Options (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1877-1895): `source` and `target` booleans, derived from `auto`, `effect`, and `list` when absent (createDrag.ts:56-57); `list`, a `read` and `splice` accessor pair the factory splices on drop, or a read-only `items` getter; `axis` (`vertical` by default, or `horizontal`); `auto` (true by default, which writes the `draggable` property); `effect.allowed` and `effect.drop`; `select` (true by default); `types`; `resolve.zone`, which can return `before`, `after`, `into`, or no position, and `resolve.indices` for a custom drag set; and `on` handlers. Events: `elements:drag:tap`, `start`, `over`, `drop`, `end`, `reorder`, `select`, and `clear` (elements/src/browser/constants.ts:407-416), each dispatched through the non-cancelable `emit` helper (elements/src/browser/helpers.ts:1530-1532); `over` and `drop` fire on the row and bubble, and the rest fire on the host. Markup: rows are direct children carrying `data-index` (helpers.ts:1767-1792); a `.drag-handle` descendant narrows the grab area and a `.no-drag` descendant opts a region out (createDrag.ts:115-132, :256-263); the factory writes the `dragging`, `selected`, `drop-target`, `drop-indicator`, `drop-indicator-before`, and `drop-indicator-after` classes (constants.ts:627-634), which elements/src/styles/composables/_drag.scss:50-102 paints. The Vue `useDrag` composable wraps the factory and turns a reactive array ref into the `list` accessor (elements/src/browser/composables/useDrag.ts:30-39).
factories.nativeFeatures: HTML drag and drop: the `draggable` property; the `dragstart`, `dragenter`, `dragover`, `dragleave`, `drop`, and `dragend` events; and `DataTransfer` with `effectAllowed`, `dropEffect`, `setData`, and `setDragImage` (createDrag.ts:92-100, :171-174, :354-383). `getBoundingClientRect` for the midpoint hit test (:78-87), `Selection.removeAllRanges` (:300), `queueMicrotask` (:138), and a capture-phase document `pointerdown` listener for click-away clearing (:415-425, :449). Reactivity comes from the `@vue/reactivity` package, not from the platform (:12).
factories.overlapReason: Bootstrap 5.3 has no reorder concept. Its `list-group` styles items with no reorder behavior (catalog-2026-10-07.md:36), and a grep of `reorder`, `draggable`, `dragover`, and `drop` (with `dropdown` excluded) over bootstrap/js/src returned 0 matches on 2026-10-07; its one drag listener is the carousel's `dragstart` blocker (bootstrap/js/src/carousel.js:45; catalog-2026-10-07.md:36). The click, Ctrl-click, and Shift-click selection model has no Bootstrap counterpart either: a list group's `.active` class marks one current item, and the Tab plugin's list-group mode shows a pane, which this factory never does.
factories.inCatalog: Shortlist rank 2, Sortable list (catalog-2026-10-07.md:25, :36), which already names this factory as guidance.
factories.lessons: Derive an item's index from its position among the host's element children, never from an attribute: elements reads `data-index` (helpers.ts:1779-1783) and relies on the framework re-rendering it after a splice (createDrag.ts:211-232), so a plugin that moves nodes with `moveBefore` would leave stale indices. Keep the midpoint hit test along one axis (createDrag.ts:78-87), and write its result as one state attribute on the target item (`before` or `after`) in place of six classes kept in step by a double pass (`queueSync`, createDrag.ts:102-139); elements' own guide requires a stylesheet reader for every state write (elements/guides/composables.md:385-394). Write the indicator only when the target or the position changes: elements emits `over` and re-syncs every row on each `dragover` (createDrag.ts:184-209, :361-367), and the platform repeats `dragover` while the pointer rests. Move the item at `drop` only, as elements does (createDrag.ts:246), and show only the indicator during `dragover`: an Escape or a release outside the host then needs no restore, because the platform cancels a native drag and fires `dragend`, which elements routes to its end event (createDrag.ts:348-352). Accept only a drag that started in the same host: elements calls `preventDefault` on every `dragenter` and `dragover` (createDrag.ts:354-367), so an OS file or text from another page becomes a valid drop with no meaning. Keep the in-host transfer in the class and decide any `text/plain` payload with the first consumer: elements writes the start index as `text/plain` (createDrag.ts:173), which a text field anywhere on the page accepts as a drop. Treat a handle as an author-written `draggable="true"` on a descendant, and call `setDragImage` with the whole item as elements does (createDrag.ts:92-100, :175), because the platform's default drag image is the dragged element, which is the handle alone. Prove the handle by a grab outside it that starts no drag: elements' showcase handle carries the class `showcase-drag-handle` (elements/app/browser/pages/UseDragDropPage.vue:294) while the factory matches only `.drag-handle` (createDrag.ts:125, :258), so that demo's rows drag from anywhere and no test caught it. Refuse a `dragstart` whose target sits in an `input`, `textarea`, `select`, or contenteditable descendant; elements leaves that to an author-written `.no-drag` class (createDrag.ts:257, :328). Keep `start` and `move` cancelable as the catalog shapes them: elements dispatches every drag event through the non-cancelable `emit` helper (helpers.ts:1530-1532), so no listener can veto a reorder, and an app that renders from data has to pass the `list` splice accessor instead (types.ts:1872-1875); a cancelable `move.vn.drag` event serves that app with no data option. Put real values in event detail: elements fabricates `new PointerEvent('pointerdown')` and similar objects with no geometry (createDrag.ts:178, :203, :241). Bind every declared handler from the event map: elements binds `on` handlers for `tap`, `start`, `over`, `drop`, `end`, and `reorder` (createDrag.ts:429-434) and never for the declared `select` and `clear` (types.ts:1864-1868), although its `bindEventMap` helper exists (helpers.ts:1558-1570). Give each method one name: elements returns `select` and `tap` as the same function (createDrag.ts:488-489). Let the scope route only the drag events and `keydown` (veneer/src/browser/Veneer.ts:66-73); elements attaches document `keydown`, `mouseup`, and `pointerdown` listeners for every instance, even while idle (createDrag.ts:447-449). Build the keyboard path from scratch: elements has no keyboard move, its only key handler is Escape during a drag (createDrag.ts:407-413), and its stylesheet header claims keyboard selection that the factory never implements (_drag.scss:4-5). Decide the axis with the first horizontal consumer: elements takes an `axis` option (types.ts:1882), and Drag 1's Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown keys assume a vertical list. Scope the fence's grab cursor and source dimming (_drag.scss:50-69) under the host attribute, because elements paints `cursor: grab` on every `[draggable='true']` element in the page (_drag.scss:50-52); take the target tint and the insertion bar (_drag.scss:76-102) from Bootstrap's color tokens. Prove the drag path with a real drag through the harness, as the catalog's probe did (catalog-2026-10-07.md:25): elements tests only the selection sub-machine and records that its drag sub-machine resists synthetic dispatch (elements/tests/src/browser/factories/createDrag.test.ts:83-92). Defer multi-selection, multi-item drags, the `into` position (types.ts:1013), and cross-list transfer to later units with their own consumers; elements' board example needs a module-level `pending` variable and a `setTimeout` clear for a cross-list move (elements/app/browser/examples/BoardExample.vue:143-178), which shows that the factory carries no transfer identity.

factories.name: createDrop
factories.capability: A page author makes any element a drop target that reports whether an accepted drag hovers it and dispatches enter, leave, and drop events. Its demos use it for OS file drops and for moving items from a `createDrag` source into a separate zone, such as an attachment tray into an outbox.
factories.api: `createDrop(element, options?)` returns `{ over, destroy }`, where `over` is a readonly boolean ref (elements/src/browser/factories/createDrop.ts:100). Options (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1952-1959): `effect.allowed` and `effect.drop`, written to `DataTransfer` on `dragenter` and `dragover` (createDrop.ts:37-41); `accept`, a list of `DataTransfer` type strings such as `Files` or `text/plain` (createDrop.ts:30-35); and `on` callbacks for `dragenter`, `dragover`, `dragleave`, and `drop` that receive the raw `DragEvent`. Events: `elements:drop:enter`, `leave`, and `drop` (elements/src/browser/constants.ts:427-431), non-cancelable, each with `detail.originalEvent` (createDrop.ts:51, :70, :79). Markup: none; any element works, and a composable layers its own tag gate (createDrop.ts:9-11). The Vue `useDrop` composable passes its options through unchanged (elements/src/browser/composables/useDrop.ts:16-38).
factories.nativeFeatures: The drag and drop target events `dragenter`, `dragover`, `dragleave`, and `drop`, with `preventDefault` to accept a drop; `DataTransfer.types`, `effectAllowed`, and `dropEffect`; and `relatedTarget` on `dragleave` with `Node.contains` to ignore moves between nested children (createDrop.ts:62-71).
factories.overlapReason: The factory serves two concepts. Dropping OS files to choose them for an upload is the file input's concept (`::file-selector-button`, bootstrap/scss/forms/_form-control.scss:95), which the catalog keeps excluded as a borderline row (catalog-2026-10-07.md:117, :157). Moving an in-page item from one list or zone into another has no Bootstrap counterpart, for the reason the sortable list passes (catalog-2026-10-07.md:36), so that half passes.
factories.inCatalog: Partly: the excluded File drop zone row (catalog-2026-10-07.md:117). Shortlist rank 2 names cross-list transfer and file drop as outside Drag 1 (catalog-2026-10-07.md:25) and plans no later unit for the transfer.
factories.proposal: Add cross-list transfer as Drag 2, a later unit of the catalog's `drags/` module, and never as a separate `drops/` module, because a drop zone with no drag source in the page is the excluded file-drop concept. Markup contract: `data-vn-drag` hosts whose attribute values match exchange items, and a host with an empty value accepts only its own items, so Drag 1 markup stays valid unchanged. The class records the dragged item and its source host at `dragstart`, calls `preventDefault` on `dragover` only for a recorded item whose source host shares the target's value, and moves the item with `moveBefore` at `drop`. Events stay in the Drag family: the target host receives the cancelable `move.vn.drag` event with `detail.from`, `detail.to`, and `detail.source` (the source host), and both hosts receive `end.vn.drag`. Styles: the Drag 1 fence's indicator, plus one rule for an empty target host, which offers no item to hit-test against. First unit: Drag 2, after Drag 1 lands, on a two-column specimen in the Native group, with a refusal proof that neither an OS file nor an item from a host with another value is accepted. Cost: medium.
factories.lessons: Ignore a `dragleave` whose `relatedTarget` sits inside the host, as elements does (createDrop.ts:62-71), but read that path in Chromium first: elements' test dispatches a synthetic `dragleave` with no `relatedTarget` (elements/tests/src/browser/factories/createDrop.test.ts:75-77), so the nested-child case is unproven there, and `relatedTarget` on drag events is unread under 141 and 153. Refuse a drag whose type list is empty: elements accepts one (createDrop.ts:33), and only a synthetic event produces it. Put extracted values in event detail, never the `DragEvent`: elements passes `originalEvent` (createDrop.ts:79), and the drag data store is readable in `dragstart` and `drop` only, because it is protected during `dragenter` and `dragover`. Couple a target to its source through the shared host value in the proposal: elements' cross-zone demo reads the source instance's `indices` ref inside the target's drop callback (elements/app/browser/pages/UseDragDropPage.vue:161-175), which ties two instances together in application code. Keep the `accept` type filter out of Drag 2, because type filtering serves the excluded file-drop concept.

factories.name: createPointer
factories.capability: A page author gets a press, move, and release gesture on an element with pointer capture, so moves and the release keep arriving after the pointer leaves the element, plus a body cursor lock and text-selection suppression for the gesture's duration. Elements composes it into toast swipe-to-dismiss and table column resizing, and its guide names splitters and sliders as further consumers (elements/guides/composables.md:432).
factories.api: `createPointer(element, options?)` returns `{ dragging, clear, destroy }`: `dragging` is a readonly boolean ref, and `clear` ends a gesture in progress and restores the body styles (elements/src/browser/factories/createPointer.ts:45-51, :107). Options (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1237-1243): `cursor`, a CSS cursor value written to `document.body` during the gesture; `accept`, a predicate that can veto a `pointerdown`; and `on.start`, `on.move`, and `on.end` callbacks that receive the raw `PointerEvent`. Events: `elements:pointer:start`, `move`, and `end` (elements/src/browser/constants.ts:577-581), non-cancelable, with `detail.originalEvent` (createPointer.ts:57, :71, :92). Markup: none; any element works (createPointer.ts:22-24). The Vue `usePointer` composable returns `dragging` and `clear` (elements/src/browser/composables/usePointer.ts:18-43).
factories.nativeFeatures: Pointer Events: `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, and `pointercancel`; `pointerId` to ignore a second pointer (createPointer.ts:76); and `setPointerCapture`, `hasPointerCapture`, and `releasePointerCapture` (:45-51, :60-72, :80). Inline `document.body.style.cursor` and `userSelect` writes, saved and restored (:40-43, :82-85).
factories.overlapReason: The factory is a mechanism with no user-facing concept of its own, so its consumers decide. Swipe-to-dismiss on a toast is Toast's concept, and a horizontal swipe on a slideshow is the engine's Swipe helper, which carries Bootstrap's touch and pen swipe recognition (veneer/src/browser/Swipe.ts:5-6; bootstrap/js/src/util/swipe.js:137). A splitter or a column resizer has no Bootstrap counterpart, which the catalog's longlist records (catalog-2026-10-07.md:78), so that use passes.
factories.inCatalog: Longlist row Split-pane resizing (catalog-2026-10-07.md:78) for the passing use; the engine's Swipe helper (catalog-2026-10-07.md:5) for the swipe uses.
factories.lessons: Keep the gesture a private part of the first module that needs it, the split-pane row when it is promoted, because the minimal-API law creates a capability only with its first real consumer (scaffold/AGENTS.md:65); elements shares its factory between two consumers, toast swipe (elements/src/browser/factories/createToast.ts:323) and column resize (elements/src/browser/factories/createTable.ts:1227-1240). Carry pointer capture on `pointerdown`, the `pointerId` guard against a second pointer, the `accept` veto for interactive descendants, and `pointercancel` handled as an end (createPointer.ts:60-93). Write a state attribute on the host and set the cursor and `user-select` in the fence, in place of inline styles on `document.body` (createPointer.ts:82-85), which overwrite an author's own inline body style for the gesture's duration. Declare `touch-action` on the gesture host in the fence: elements leaves it to each consumer's stylesheet (elements/guides/composables.md:409), and on a touch host without it the browser can claim the gesture for panning and send `pointercancel`. Pair the gesture with a keyboard path: elements' column resize takes pointer input only (createTable.ts:1227-1240), and the catalog's split-pane row names the missing keyboard splitter (catalog-2026-10-07.md:78). Prove capture with a real pointer drag that leaves the host: elements' tests dispatch synthetic `pointerdown` and `pointerup` on the host itself (elements/tests/src/browser/factories/createPointer.test.ts:21-34), which never exercises capture.

factories.name: createFocus
factories.capability: A page author confines Tab and Shift+Tab to a container's focusable descendants while a trap is active, focuses an initial element on activation, and restores the earlier focus on deactivation. Its guide names drawer-like surfaces without native focus management as the use (elements/guides/composables.md:429); a grep of the factories folder on 2026-10-07 finds no other factory that composes it.
factories.api: `createFocus(element, options?)` returns `{ active, activate, deactivate, destroy }`, with `active` a readonly boolean ref (elements/src/browser/factories/createFocus.ts:97-102). Options (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1976-1983): `initial`, an element or a function of the host that returns the element to focus, defaulting to the first focusable descendant; and `restore`, true by default, which focuses the earlier active element on deactivation (createFocus.ts:68-85). Events: `elements:focus:activate` and `elements:focus:deactivate` (elements/src/browser/constants.ts:439-442), non-cancelable. Markup: none; candidates match `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` (constants.ts:154-155) minus elements that carry a `disabled` attribute (createFocus.ts:44-47). The Vue `useFocus` composable returns `active`, `activate`, and `deactivate` (elements/src/browser/composables/useFocus.ts:21-47).
factories.nativeFeatures: `document.activeElement`, `HTMLElement.focus`, and a document `keydown` listener for Tab with `preventDefault` (createFocus.ts:49-66); a CSS selector list for focusable candidates (constants.ts:154-155).
factories.overlapReason: A focus trap is the concept of the engine's Trap helper, which carries Bootstrap's `util/focustrap.js` (veneer/src/browser/Trap.ts:11; bootstrap/js/src/util/focustrap.js:19-22, :99-111), and the catalog excludes the borrowed Tab wrap on that ground (catalog-2026-10-07.md:93). A trap with no surface around it has no user-facing concept of its own, and every surface elements names for it, a drawer or a dialog, is Offcanvas's or Modal's.
factories.inCatalog: Excluded row Bare `dialog` with the borrowed Tab wrap, whose counterpart is the Trap helper (catalog-2026-10-07.md:93).
factories.lessons: None for the native track: Trap owns the concept. Two readings let a reviewer compare the two traps, and neither one asks for a change. Trap pulls escaped focus back on `focusin` with the last Tab direction (veneer/src/browser/Trap.ts:50-59, :75-86), so focus that leaves by pointer or by script returns; elements wraps only when Tab leaves the first or the last candidate (createFocus.ts:49-64), attaches its document listener at construction even while inactive (:66), and filters candidates by the `disabled` attribute only, never by visibility or `inert` (:44-47). The `initial` and `restore` options (types.ts:1976-1983) are elements' only additions, and in Bootstrap the family returns focus to its trigger after hiding (bootstrap/js/src/modal.js:352-354; bootstrap/js/src/offcanvas.js:243-246), not the trap.

factories.name: useAlert
factories.capability: A page author shows and dismisses an alert, with cancelable show and hide events and a descendant dismiss control. The Vue composable resolves a template ref and delegates to `createAlert`.
factories.api: `useAlert(elementRef, options?)` returns `visible`, `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` (elements/src/browser/composables/useAlert.ts:17-44). `createAlert` options are `initial` (visible by default) and `on` (elements/src/browser/types.ts:2037-2046); it emits cancelable `elements:alert:show` and `hide` and post-transition `open` and `close`, mirrors `[data-alert-open]` and `aria-hidden`, and dismisses on a click inside a `[data-alert-dismiss]` descendant (elements/src/browser/factories/createAlert.ts:6-17; elements/src/browser/constants.ts:620-623). Markup: a host with `role="alert"` or `role="status"`; the factory adds `role="alert"` when the role is absent (useAlert.ts:10-13).
factories.nativeFeatures: The `role` and `aria-hidden` attributes, a delegated `click` listener, and a CSS transition wait through the `runTransition` helper (createAlert.ts:4).
factories.overlapReason: A dismissible alert is Bootstrap's Alert component, which the engine ships (veneer/src/browser/Alert.ts:7); elements states that `[data-alert-dismiss]` replaces `.btn-close` (constants.ts:620-623), which changes the hook only.
factories.inCatalog: No row; Alert is one of the drop-in families the ruling names (catalog-2026-10-07.md:5).
factories.lessons: None for the native track.

factories.name: useAside
factories.capability: A page author opens and closes an `aside` drawer as a native popover, with light dismiss, a backdrop, and a slide animation driven by CSS. The composable resolves a template ref and delegates to `createAside`.
factories.api: `useAside(elementRef, options?)` returns `visible`, `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` (elements/src/browser/composables/useAside.ts:20-50). `createAside` options are `popover` (`auto` by default, `manual`, or false to keep the authored value) and `on` (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1525-1536); it bridges `beforetoggle` to `elements:aside:show` and `hide` and `toggle` to `open` and `close`, all non-cancelable, and maps `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` to `showPopover`, `hidePopover`, and `togglePopover` (elements/src/browser/factories/createAside.ts:18-33). Markup: the host must be an `aside` element, and the factory throws otherwise (createAside.ts:53).
factories.nativeFeatures: The `popover` attribute with `showPopover`, `hidePopover`, and `togglePopover`; the `beforetoggle` and `toggle` events; `:popover-open`, `::backdrop`, `@starting-style`, and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (createAside.ts:7-16).
factories.overlapReason: A drawer that slides over the page is Offcanvas (veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:21), and the catalog excludes the manual-popover offcanvas and `dialog class="offcanvas"` because both replace the offcanvas host (catalog-2026-10-07.md:102).
factories.inCatalog: Excluded row `dialog class="offcanvas"` and the manual-popover offcanvas (catalog-2026-10-07.md:102).
factories.lessons: None for the drawer. One reading applies to every native module with a fence: never wait for a transition that the stylesheet does not declare. Elements removed a `transitionend` wait from this factory that its guide reports at about 400 ms per close, against about 73 ms after the removal (createAside.ts:35-42; elements/guides/composables.md:389), so Fullscreen, Editor, and Drag take their state from the platform event and leave motion to the fence.

factories.name: useButton
factories.capability: A page author gets a toggle button whose pressed state mirrors between the `.active` class and a reactive value, with a toggle event on each click.
factories.api: `useButton(elementRef, options?)` returns `active` and `toggle` (elements/src/browser/composables/useButton.ts:15-40). `createButton` takes `on` only (elements/src/browser/types.ts:2009-2011), dispatches `elements:button:toggle` with `detail.active` on each click, and seeds its state from the class without an event (elements/src/browser/factories/createButton.ts:6-17). Markup: the host must be a `button` element (createButton.ts:11-13).
factories.nativeFeatures: The `aria-pressed` attribute and a `click` listener (createButton.ts:6-14).
factories.overlapReason: A pressed toggle is Bootstrap's Button toggle (veneer/src/browser/Button.ts:7), and the catalog excludes the native pressed toggle on that ground (catalog-2026-10-07.md:122).
factories.inCatalog: Excluded row The native pressed toggle and the checkbox `switch` attribute (catalog-2026-10-07.md:122).
factories.lessons: None for the native track. Fullscreen 1 and Wake 1 mirror `aria-pressed` on their `command` triggers (catalog-2026-10-07.md:26, :31); keep that mirror inside each module and never route it through the engine's Button, which owns `.active` toggling.

factories.name: useCarousel
factories.capability: A page author runs a slideshow with an active index, autoplay that pauses on hover, arrow-key navigation, wrap, and touch swipe, while authoring the slide markup and the transition CSS.
factories.api: `useCarousel(elementRef, options?)` returns `index`, `cycling`, `next`, `prev`, `to`, `start`, `stop`, `pause`, and `resume` (elements/src/browser/composables/useCarousel.ts:20-53). `createCarousel` options: `autoplay.interval`, `autoplay.pause` (`hover` or false), `autoplay.ride` (`mount`, `interaction`, or false), `keyboard`, `wrap`, `touch`, and `on` (elements/src/browser/types.ts:2178-2188). Markup: an `ol` or `ul` of `li` or `[role="listitem"]` items and optional indicator buttons in a `[role="tablist"]` wrapper; the factory writes `.active` and the `.carousel-item-next`, `.carousel-item-prev`, `.carousel-item-start`, and `.carousel-item-end` classes (elements/src/browser/factories/createCarousel.ts:12-28).
factories.nativeFeatures: `setInterval`, `keydown` with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, a `touchstart` swipe, and `aria-selected` on indicators (a grep of createCarousel.ts on 2026-10-07).
factories.overlapReason: A slideshow is Bootstrap's Carousel (veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:25), and the factory writes Bootstrap's own `.carousel-item-*` transition classes (createCarousel.ts:22-27).
factories.inCatalog: Excluded row Scroll snap with `::scroll-button` and `::scroll-marker`, which rules any slideshow the Carousel concept (catalog-2026-10-07.md:106).
factories.lessons: None for the native track.

factories.name: useDetails
factories.capability: A page author gets a `details` disclosure with cancelable show and hide events and accordion behavior, where opening one panel closes its open siblings.
factories.api: `useDetails(elementRef, options?)` returns `visible`, `show`, `hide`, and `toggle` (elements/src/browser/composables/useDetails.ts:18-49). `createDetails` options: `initial`, `accordion` (a container element), and `on` (elements/src/browser/types.ts:1485-1491); it emits cancelable `elements:details:show` and `hide` and coordinates siblings by dispatching `elements:details:deactivate` on them (elements/src/browser/factories/createDetails.ts:6-21). Markup: the host must be a `details` element (createDetails.ts:23).
factories.nativeFeatures: The `details` element's `open` attribute and its `beforetoggle` and `toggle` events, with motion left to an authored `interpolate-size` and `::details-content` transition (createDetails.ts:12-17).
factories.overlapReason: Showing and hiding a region, alone or in an accordion group, is Collapse and Accordion (veneer/src/browser/Collapse.ts:22), and the catalog excludes `details` with `name` groups on that ground (catalog-2026-10-07.md:94).
factories.inCatalog: Excluded row `details` and `summary` with `name` groups, `::details-content`, and the `toggle` event (catalog-2026-10-07.md:94).
factories.lessons: None for the native track.

factories.name: useDialog
factories.capability: A page author opens a `dialog` as a modal or non-modal window with cancelable show and hide events, an Escape and backdrop dismissal policy, and an optional body scroll lock for the non-modal case.

The case for a pass is that Bootstrap 5.3 has no leave-page concept, and the warning is the browser's own `beforeunload` prompt, which a Bootstrap Modal can't show because a modal can't intercept a tab close or a reload. The case against is the catalog's notifications precedent, which ruled a message outside the page to be the toast concept (`catalog:128`). Support: `beforeunload` is Chrome 1 and not Baseline (see [web-features 3.40.1](https://unpkg.com/web-features/data.json), read 2026-10-07, local copy `scratchpad/wf/data.json`); the Chromium-only target sets the non-Baseline status aside, as it does for Fullscreen (`catalog:26`). With no trigger, the plugin boots every host through the boot entry (`veneer/src/browser/types.ts:2047-2053`) and routes `input`, `change`, `submit`, and `reset`. The class derives dirty state from the platform's defaults instead of storing a flag: a form is dirty while a control's `value` differs from its `defaultValue`, `checked` from `defaultChecked`, or an option's `selected` from `defaultSelected`, so typing a value back clears it. While the form is dirty, the class holds one `beforeunload` listener on the window that calls `preventDefault`. It removes the listener when the form turns clean, submits, resets, or disconnects. The host receives `change.vn.guard` after each transition, with `detail.dirty`. Chromium shows the prompt only after a user gesture on the page, which the edit that dirties the form supplies; web-features 3.40.1 lists `api.Window.beforeunload_event.preventdefault_activation` under the `beforeunload` feature. No CSS. First unit: Guard 1, which covers the module, its tests, and a Native group specimen where an edit arms the prompt and a restore, a submit, or a reset disarms it. factories.lessons:
The reset timing is the lesson that carries the most weight, and it changes Output 1 (`catalog:42`). `createForm` re-reads its snapshot in a microtask that its `reset` listener queues (`createForm.ts:326-338`). Under Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and 153.0.8010.12, a trusted click on a reset button runs that microtask before the controls revert, so the microtask reads the old value. A scripted `form.reset()` runs it after the controls revert (`scratchpad/elements-lane/reset.ts`, run 2026-10-07: click gave `microtask:beta`, scripted gave `microtask:alpha`). The factory's snapshot after a reset-button click therefore holds stale data. The same run shows that the native reset restores `output.defaultValue` on both paths (`readout-of-alpha`). Output 1 can set `output.defaultValue` at boot to the readout of the control's `defaultValue` and drop its `reset` route, because the platform then resets the control and the readout together. - Form submission: the `formdata` bridge (`createForm.ts:310-314`) gives a later Editor unit a native path. An `Editor` inside a form can add its text in the form's `formdata` event instead of mirroring into a hidden input.

factories.proposal: Sortable table columns. Shape: folder `veneer/src/browser/sorters/`, entity `Sorter`, host `table[data-vn-sorter]` with one `tbody`. Trigger: a `button` of type `button` inside each sortable `th`, the markup of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices example (see [APG sortable table example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/examples/sortable-table/)). Enter and Space reach that button as native clicks, so the plugin routes `click` alone, and the route's `hosts` function resolves the closest `table[data-vn-sorter]` (`veneer/src/browser/types.ts:2042`). State lives in the DOM: the sorted header carries `aria-sort` set to `ascending` or `descending`, and no other header carries it, because ARIA has authors apply `aria-sort` to one header at a time (see [WAI-ARIA 1.2, aria-sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-sort)). A click on an unsorted column sorts ascending, and a click on the sorted column flips the direction. A cell's sort key is the `value` of a `data` element or the `datetime` of a `time` element it holds, else its text. Keys compare through `Intl.Collator` in the table's closest `lang`, with `numeric: true`. The plugin moves rows with `moveBefore`, which keeps focus inside a moved row where `appendChild` drops it (`scratchpad/elements-lane/move.ts`, run 2026-10-07 under Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and 153.0.8010.12: after `appendChild` focus sat on `body`, after `moveBefore` it stayed on the row's button). Events on the host: `sort.vn.sorter` (cancelable, before the move, with `detail.column` and `detail.direction`) and `change.vn.sorter` (after the move). A polite live region reports the column and direction, as Drag 1 and Filter 1 report theirs (`catalog:36`, `:40`). Sorter 1 sorts plain rows. It refuses a body that holds a `rowspan` cell with a coded refusal in core (`records/native-separation-verdict.md:52`), because a move would split the spanning row. One fence rule draws the direction mark from `aria-sort`. Support: `move-before` Chrome 133, not Baseline; `data` Baseline high since 2020-04-24; `Intl.Collator` sits in the `intl` feature, Baseline high since 2020-03-28 (see [web-features 3.40.1](https://unpkg.com/web-features/data.json), read 2026-10-07). First unit: Sorter 1, which covers the module, its tests, and a Native group specimen built from the carriers data in the showcase tables section (`veneer/app/browser/sections/tables.html:46-76`), sorting its Trucks and On time columns. The specimen copies that data so the Bootstrap table specimen keeps its Bootstrap-only markup. Cost: small.
factories.lessons:
These ideas carry into Sorter, and the defects after them are the ones Sorter's shape avoids:
- Stable ties: the sort carries each row's prior ordinal as the last tie-break, so equal keys keep their order (`createTable.ts:784-805`).
- Server paging: `sort.auto: false` lets a server-paged table refetch instead of moving rows (`createTable.ts:110-114`). In Sorter that is a listener that prevents `sort.vn.sorter`.
- Formatted cells: a separate sort value per cell (`createTable.ts:794-800`) is right. The native `data` and `time` elements carry that value without a custom attribute.
- Focusable headers: the factory makes the `th` itself focusable with `tabindex` and handles Enter and Space on it (`createTable.ts:349-367`, `:1341-1348`). A `button` inside the header gives those keys natively and exposes an actionable role, so Sorter takes the button.
- Detail rows: the in-place sort collects every row of the first `tbody`, detail rows included (`createTable.ts:771`, `:786`), so a sort separates an expansion row from its parent. A later Sorter unit that admits grouped rows must move each group as one.
- Lost focus: the factory reorders with `appendChild` (`createTable.ts:810`), which drops focus inside a moved row, per the same `move.ts` reading.
- Several sorted headers: multiple-column sort writes `aria-sort` on more than one header at a time (`createTable.ts:823-859`), against the ARIA rule the proposal cites. Leave multiple-column sort out.
- Dead fields: `TableColumn.sort`, `filter`, and `filterable` (`types.ts:2326-2330`) have no reader in `createTable.ts`, which compares through `compareCellValues` alone (`createTable.ts:801`). Declare a comparator hook only with its first consumer.
- Column resizing: the factory pairs a pointer handle per header with clamped widths (`createTable.ts:1170-1250`) and has no keyboard path. A later resize module must add one, as the catalog's split-pane row notes (`catalog:78`).
- Inert panels: the detail panel uses `inert` instead of `hidden` so a CSS height transition can run (`createTable.ts:1034-1040`). That technique serves Collapse's concept and stays off the native track.

factories.lessons:
These ideas carry into Filter 1 (`catalog:40`) and Editor 1 (`catalog:46`), neither of which touches the select concept:

- Drop position: before or after by the row's midpoint on the list axis (`createDrag.ts:78-87`), with an `axis` choice for horizontal lists. Drag 1 takes the midpoint rule and leaves out `into`, which serves nesting.
- Flicker: `dragleave` clears the target only when `relatedTarget` leaves the host (`createDrag.ts:369-376`; `createDrop.ts:62-71`), because the platform fires `dragleave` at every child boundary.
- Drag image: anchoring `setDragImage` at the pointer's offset inside the row (`createDrag.ts:92-100`) keeps the preview under the cursor.
- Cancellation: Escape ends a drag, and `end` carries `cancelled: true` (`createDrag.ts:147-150`, `:407-413`). Drag 1's `end.vn.drag` can carry the same flag.
- Multiple items: when several indices move, the insert point drops by the count of moved items that sat before it (`createDrag.ts:211-232`); a later multiple-selection Drag unit needs that arithmetic.
The factory also leaves gaps that Drag 1 must close:
- Keyboard: the only key the factory handles is Escape (`createDrag.ts:407-413`), so Drag 1's Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown moves, focus retention, and live region have no precedent here.
- DOM moves: the factory splices the consumer's array and relies on a framework to re-render (`createDrag.ts:211-232`), so with no `list` nothing reorders. Drag 1 moves the nodes with `moveBefore`, which keeps focus where `appendChild` drops it (`scratchpad/elements-lane/move.ts`, run 2026-10-07 under Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and 153.0.8010.12).
- Positional identity: each row carries an authored `data-index` that the consumer must rewrite after every move (`helpers.ts:1779-1783`). Drag 1 derives position from the DOM.
- Synthetic details: the `start`, `over`, and `drop` details carry a `PointerEvent` built with no coordinates (`createDrag.ts:178`, `:203`, `:241`). Drag 1 must put real values in its details or leave the field out.
- Unbound handlers: the types declare `on.select` and `on.clear` (`types.ts:1864-1868`), and the factory never binds them (`createDrag.ts:429-434`).
- Untested path: the tests cover selection only and state that `dragstart` through `drop` resists synthetic dispatch (`elements/tests/src/browser/factories/createDrag.test.ts:83-89`); no test drives a drop or a reorder. Drag 1's proof must drive a real pointer drag, as the catalog's `dragstart` and `drop` probe did under 153 (`catalog:25`).
- Touch: the factory has no touch path. A touch fallback would compose pointer capture as `createPointer` does (`createPointer.ts:74-93`), and the catalog records Android touch drag as unread (`catalog:36`).

The plugin routes `click` on a header button, alternates that column between ascending and descending, writes `aria-sort` on that header and removes it from the others, which follows the one-sorted-header rule (see [WAI-ARIA 1.2, aria-sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-sort)), and moves the rows of the table's first `tbody` element with `moveBefore` in a stable order, comparing numbers numerically and text with `Intl.Collator` in the language of the closest `lang` attribute. Events on the table: `sort.vn.sorter` (cancelable, before the rows move, with `detail.key` and `detail.direction`; prevention leaves the rows and `aria-sort` unchanged) and `change.vn.sorter` (after the rows move). Styles: one fence rule draws the direction caret on `th[aria-sort] button`. First unit, Sorter 1: single-column sort on the showcase's Shipment table (veneer/app/browser/sections/tables.html:5-13), with no multi-column sort, no unsorted state, and no server mode; a Native group specimen; cost small.
factories.lessons: Take the comparison and the stable order: numbers compare numerically when both cells parse, text compares through `Intl.Collator` (elements/src/browser/helpers.ts:1340-1354), an explicit per-cell sort value wins over the visible text (createTable.ts:794-800), and ties keep their prior order through an ordinal (createTable.ts:784-805). Put a `button` element inside each sortable header instead of the factory's `tabindex="0"` on the `th` element with a hand-written Enter and Space handler (createTable.ts:340-367, 1341-1348); the button brings the role, the focus stop, and keyboard activation. Move rows with `moveBefore` rather than `appendChild` (createTable.ts:807-810), so a row's focused control keeps focus. Write `aria-sort` on the sorted header only: the factory seeds `aria-sort="none"` on every sortable header (createTable.ts:357-360) and writes one value per sorted column in multi-sort. Keep the factory's event-only mode for server-paged data (createTable.ts:110-114; elements/src/browser/types.ts:2404-2410) for a later unit. The arrow-key cell focus (createTable.ts:1289-1316) and the column resize also pass the overlap test, but each is a larger unit with no showcase consumer.

factories.lessons: Keep the event pair in every native module: a cancelable event before the platform acts and a non-cancelable notification after it settles (elements/src/browser/constants.ts:26-28). The catalog applies that pair as `copy` and `result` for the Copier and as `enter` and `change` for the Fullscreen (catalog-2026-10-07.md:34, :38).
